newsitem.title: JAPAN: Refinery loading unaffected by Tokyo Bay oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Refinery loading unaffected by Tokyo Bay oil spill.

text.p: Loading and unloading operations at oil refineries on the Tokyo Bay coast have not been affected by an oil spill from a supertanker, which struck a reef in the bay on Wednesday morning, refinery officials said.

"Refinery operations, including loading and off-loading, have not been disrupted by the spill," said a spokesman for Showa Shell Sekiyu KK, which runs a 120,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Kawasaki.

Operations at other refineries nearby, including Nippon Oil Co Ltd's 385,000 bpd plant, Cosmo Oil Co Ltd's 240,000 bpd refinery and Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd's 250,000 bpd plant, have not been affected by the oil spill, company spokesmen said.
Refinery spokesmen also said shipping routes may be blocked by oil fences if the oil slick, spreading over an area about 5.5 km (3.4 miles) long and 4.5 km (2.8 miles) wide, expands further.

Japan's coastguard said the 259,999 deadweight-tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace, which scraped a reef in shallow waters of Tokyo Bay on Wednesday morning, was estimated to have leaked 13,400 tonnes of crude oil.
The vessel was on its way to Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's Kawasaki plant, south of Tokyo.
